title: Telangana CM Presses US Ambassador for Faster H-1B Processing and Visa Slots
excerpt: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy met US Ambassador Sergio Gor in New Delhi, urging streamlined H-1B renewals, more visa interview slots, and advance notice on policy changes affecting Indian professionals.
body:
• Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy met US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor in New Delhi on August 5 for a 30-minute meeting focused on visa delays and bilateral ties.
  • Reddy urged faster H-1B processing, streamlined renewals and visa stamping, more interview slots, and advance notice before any US visa regulation changes.
  • The meeting comes amid heightened tension over US immigration policy, including a proposed $100,000 fee on post-graduation work permits and the earlier H-1B fee hike struck down by courts.
  • Ambassador Gor assured full cooperation in expanding Telangana-US relations across trade, investment, and cultural exchanges.

Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy used a meeting with US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor on August 5 to press for relief on visa processing delays that have frustrated Indian professionals and students across the state.

The 30-minute meeting in New Delhi covered a range of issues from H-1B renewals to student visa backlogs, with Reddy making pointed requests for concrete changes rather than broad assurances.

Specific Demands on H-1B and Student Visas

Reddy asked the ambassador to streamline the H-1B visa process, renewals, and visa stamping procedures to eliminate delays. He requested that Washington provide advance notice before implementing changes to visa regulations — a sore point for Indian professionals who have been caught off-guard by abrupt policy shifts under the Trump administration.

On student visas, the Chief Minister sought an increase in the number of US visas issued to Telangana students pursuing higher education and asked for more visa interview slots and faster appointment availability.

"He requested that the H-1B visa process, renewals, and visa stamping procedures be streamlined to avoid delays. He also suggested that advance notice be provided regarding any changes to US visa regulations."

— Telangana Chief Minister's Office statement

Why Telangana's Voice Carries Weight

Telangana, home to Hyderabad's sprawling IT corridor, is one of India's largest source states for H-1B workers and international students bound for the US. The state's tech industry — anchored by companies like Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and scores of Indian IT firms — relies heavily on cross-border talent mobility.

Reddy underscored this by pitching Telangana as a destination for US investment in IT, artificial intelligence, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, startups, and emerging technologies. He noted that Telugu is one of the fastest-growing Indian languages in the United States, a reflection of the deep professional ties between the state and the US.

Backdrop of Policy Turmoil

The meeting took place against a charged backdrop. In September 2025, Reddy had publicly urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar to address the Trump administration's $100,000 H-1B visa fee on a "war footing," calling it "totally unacceptable in the historical context of Indo-American relationships." That fee was later struck down by federal courts.

Since then, the administration has continued tightening immigration policy. A new rule ending Duration of Status — which allowed international students to remain in the US for the length of their studies — takes effect September 15, 2026, imposing a four-year cap with extensions subject to approval. The Wall Street Journal has also reported that the administration is considering a $100,000 fee on Optional Practical Training, the post-graduation work program.

For Indian professionals already in the US on H-1B visas, renewal and stamping delays have been a persistent problem. Many face months-long waits for appointments at US consulates in India, creating uncertainty about whether they can return to their jobs after home visits.

Ambassador's Response

Ambassador Gor offered a general assurance of cooperation. According to the Telangana CMO, Gor "assured the Chief Minister of full cooperation in further strengthening trade, investment, cultural exchanges, and people-to-people ties between Telangana and the United States."

The meeting also covered the safety and welfare of Telangana students studying in the US, and proposals to expand university collaborations, student exchange programs, and research partnerships.

Immigration Hawks Push Back

The meeting drew attention from US immigration restrictionists. The US Tech Workers advocacy group posted on X: "The Trump admin finally stopped rubber-stamping student visas plagued by fraud (especially from India). Now Indian officials are lobbying @USAmbIndia to reverse it. America First means holding the line."

For the Indian diaspora, the tension highlights a familiar squeeze: state governments in India lobbying on behalf of their citizens abroad while the US tightens the pathways that generations of Indian professionals have relied on to build careers in America.

nri_angle: H-1B processing delays and visa stamping backlogs directly affect tens of thousands of Indian tech workers in the US, many from Telangana. The state's push for streamlined renewals reflects the frustrations of Indian professionals navigating an increasingly hostile US immigration environment.
author: Diaspora Desk
